## 1. PCI PM callbacks that reach `i915_pm_suspend`

`drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c` — `const struct dev_pm_ops i915_pm_ops`:

```
.suspend  = i915_pm_suspend      <-- PCI/PM core: dpm_suspend()
.poweroff = i915_pm_suspend      <-- PCI/PM core: hibernate poweroff phase
```

Those are the **only two** `dev_pm_ops` entries bound to `i915_pm_suspend`. Every other slot has its own distinct entry point:

```
.prepare        = i915_pm_prepare
.suspend        = i915_pm_suspend        ──┐
.suspend_late   = i915_pm_suspend_late     │ both alias the same fn
.suspend_noirq  = i915_pm_suspend_noirq    │
.poweroff       = i915_pm_suspend        ──┘
.poweroff_late  = i915_pm_poweroff_late
.poweroff_noirq = i915_pm_poweroff_noirq
.freeze / .freeze_late / .thaw / .thaw_early
.resume / .resume_early / .restore / .restore_early / .complete
.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend
```

Full chain from the PCI layer down:

```
PCI/PM core (pci_pm_suspend / pci_pm_poweroff)
  └─ i915_pm_ops.suspend | i915_pm_ops.poweroff
       └─ i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
            ├─ i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
            ├─ early-out if i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF
            └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

The sibling late/noirq legs (for completeness, since they share `i915_drm_suspend_late`):

```
i915_pm_suspend_late   -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false)
i915_pm_suspend_noirq  -> i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, false)
i915_pm_poweroff_late  -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true)
i915_pm_poweroff_noirq -> i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, true)
i915_pm_freeze         -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm) + i915_gem_freeze(i915)
i915_pm_freeze_late    -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true) + i915_gem_freeze_late(i915)
i915_driver_shutdown   -> (via i915_pci_shutdown, .shutdown in i915_pci.c) — separate path, does NOT call i915_pm_suspend
```

## 2. Which of those callers also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

**None — the symbol `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` does not exist in this tree.**

`rtk grep i915_pm_runtime` returns no matches anywhere under `drivers/gpu/drm/i915`. The runtime-PM hook is named **`intel_runtime_suspend`**:

```
i915_pm_ops.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend
static int intel_runtime_suspend(struct device *kdev)
     ├─ i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)
     ├─ intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(dev_priv->pxp)
     └─ for_each_gt: intel_gt_runtime_suspend(gt)
```

It is a *peer* of `i915_pm_suspend` in the same `dev_pm_ops` table, not a callee/caller of it — there is no edge in either direction between the system-suspend chain and the runtime-suspend chain. So the answer to "which callers of `i915_pm_suspend` also call the runtime variant" is: **the empty set**.

## 3. Data flow of `dev_priv` from `i915_drm_suspend` to the display suspend

Note: `intel_display_suspend` has also been renamed in this tree; the reachable function is **`intel_display_driver_suspend`** (`display/intel_display_driver.c`, declared in `intel_display_driver.h`). `rtk grep intel_display_suspend` matches nothing in `intel_display.c`, `intel_display_driver.c`, or `intel_modeset_setup.c`.

The pointer chain:

```
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
│   struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);
│                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ device -> drm_i915_private
└──> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
     │                  ^^^^^^^^ passed as embedded struct drm_device *
     │
     │  struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);   // container_of back out
     │  struct intel_display    *display  = dev_priv->display;
     │                                      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ i915_drv.h:
     │                                        struct intel_display *display;
     │
     ├─ drm_client_dev_suspend(dev)              // uses drm_device
     ├─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display)    // dev_priv dropped here,
     │       │                                   // only intel_display survives
     │       └─ drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
     │                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^ back to drm_device
     ├─ intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv)
     ├─ intel_display_driver_suspend_access(display)
     ├─ intel_encoder_suspend_all(display)
     └─ intel_dmc_suspend(display)               // before GGTT suspend
```

Summary of the transformation: `struct device *kdev` → `drm_i915_private *i915` (`kdev_to_i915`) → `struct drm_device *` (`&i915->drm`) → back to `dev_priv` (`to_i915(dev)`) → narrowed to `dev_priv->display` (`struct intel_display *`), which is what the display-side suspend entry points consume. `dev_priv` itself is **not** forwarded into the display layer; it is projected down to its `->display` member, and the display code re-derives the DRM device via `display->drm` when it needs the atomic helpers.
